incidents.victim: Government, military and political figures in Ukraine, Europe and the US
incidents.vector: Social engineering rather than app exploits — texts impersonating messaging-platform support tricked targets into surrendering account credentials and one-time codes.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's SBU, working with the FBI, exposed a long-running campaign hijacking Signal, WhatsApp and Telegram accounts of officials to access sensitive military, political and economic communications.

incidents.victim: Government and military organizations in Ukraine; entities tied to Italian foreign policy
incidents.vector: Deployment of a custom .NET backdoor (STOCKSTAY) disguised as a stock-market viewer/PDF/calculator app, communicating over encrypted WebSocket C2.
incidents.impact: Google's GTIG detailed a Russian state espionage backdoor in continuous use since 2022 for command execution, file theft and screen capture against Ukrainian and Italian-interest targets.

incidents.victim: Government and state-owned energy/critical-infrastructure entities in Southeast Asia
incidents.vector: ASPX web shells on exploited web apps, then SoftEther VPN/VNT tunneling, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato and a new custom backdoor (TinyRCT) for command execution and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Unit 42 tracked a Chinese-speaking cluster compromising at least ten SE Asian organizations, exfiltrating government databases and web-server source code and breaching two state-owned energy operators.

incidents.victim: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM) deployments worldwide
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-20230, an unauthenticated SSRF in the WebDialer service chained to drop JSP web shells and escalate to root.
incidents.impact: Attackers weaponized a public proof-of-concept within 24 hours, hitting decoy CUCM systems; organizations with WebDialer enabled and unpatched are urged to assume scanning/compromise.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party vendor that loaded malicious code onto the Polymarket website.
incidents.impact: The prediction-market platform said attackers stole roughly $3 million before detection; it pledged to reimburse affected users.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion disrupting IT systems for logistics and accounting; a related regional dairy site was defaced with fabricated contamination claims.
incidents.impact: The Ufa-based manufacturer was forced to process shipments and paperwork manually, the latest in a string of cyberattacks on Russia's dairy sector.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed vector knocking out customer-facing services.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's national postal service lost its mobile app and parts of its web services and worked to restore operations.

incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing of reused passwords against ~60,000 accounts; access resold via cybercrime marketplaces.
incidents.impact: Minnesota operator 'Snoopy' (Nathan Austad) was sentenced to 18 months and over $1.3M restitution — the third and final defendant sentenced in the ~$600K DraftKings credential-stuffing scheme.

incidents.vector: Rogue SD-WAN peering (via CVE-2026-20127/20182) then a zero-day in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (CVE-2026-20245) to create a rogue root 'troot' account.
incidents.impact: Mandiant found attackers gained root-level control of a provider's SD-WAN control plane in early 2026, with extensive anti-forensic cleanup leaving the full scope of internal-traffic access unclear.

incidents.vector: Coordinated court-ordered takedown (RICO) of shared C2 infrastructure behind an infostealer (StealC), a loader (Amadey) and a dropper (SocGholish).
incidents.impact: Microsoft and Europol seized 326 servers and 142 domains, reclaimed 27M+ stolen credentials and €41M in crypto; the tools were tied to 140,000+ infected machines and feed ransomware and espionage operations.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting the automaker and its technology subsidiary; threat actor and data-theft status undisclosed.
incidents.impact: One of India's largest vehicle makers disclosed the incident in a regulatory filing, saying containment was so far 'successful,' amid a wave of attacks on major Indian manufacturers.

incidents.vector: Breach of a public email service also used by five other Japanese ISPs.
incidents.impact: Hackers reportedly accessed data of more than 14 million users of KDDI's email platform.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a contractor managing the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a wave of Ivanti EPMM server attacks.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officers were stolen — exposing sensitive personnel data of a national security agency.

incidents.vector: USB drives infected with Chinese malware connected to classified military networks.
incidents.impact: Japan's military reportedly used malware-laden USB drives on classified networks; the breach went undisclosed for nearly a year, and officials are notifying NATO partners of a possible leak.

incidents.vector: Data theft and extortion; the World Leaks group claims it stole 200,000+ documents.
incidents.impact: The Indian manufacturer confirmed a cyberattack after the extortion group published files allegedly containing sensitive Apple and Tesla component data (authenticity not independently verified).

incidents.victim: Transport for London, Marks & Spencer, Co-op, US healthcare providers (Scattered Spider; guilty pleas)
incidents.vector: Voice/SMS phishing and SIM-swapping to steal employee single sign-on credentials, enabling intrusions and ransom attacks.
incidents.impact: Two UK members of the Scattered Spider group pleaded guilty over the Aug 2024 TfL attack; US prosecutors tie the wider group to 120 intrusions of 47 entities and $115M+ in ransom payments.

incidents.victim: LastPass and other Salesforce customers (via Klue)
incidents.vector: A 2022 pilot credential at market-research firm Klue was reused to steal data from its customers' Salesforce instances.
incidents.impact: LastPass and several cybersecurity companies confirmed data taken from their Salesforce accounts via the Klue breach, part of an expanding wave of Salesforce-targeted data thefts.

incidents.victim: Check Point Remote Access VPN customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-50751, a CVSS 9.3 authentication bypass (IKEv1 certificate-validation logic error) allowing fully authenticated VPN sessions without a password.
incidents.impact: A Qilin ransomware affiliate exploited the flaw from early May — roughly six weeks before the June 21 CISA directive — compromising dozens of organizations using Rclone exfiltration and Tox-based C2.

incidents.vector: Mass brute-forcing and exploitation of old FortiOS flaws, plus a custom 'FortigateSniffer' intercepting credentials across 24 protocols, with GPU-cluster hash cracking and follow-on AD access.
incidents.impact: Valid admin/VPN credentials for tens of thousands of FortiGate devices across government, telecom, finance and critical infrastructure were exposed; a Turkish NATO defense contractor reportedly had classified documents stolen. Infrastructure remains active.

incidents.vector: Destructive cyberattack of undisclosed vector against banking systems.
incidents.impact: Intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely behind an attack that crippled Iranian banks earlier in June, amid heightened regional tensions.

incidents.victim: Universities and other Oracle PeopleSoft customers (ShinyHunters extortion)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-35273), added to CISA's KEV catalog on evidence of active exploitation.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters group has been actively extorting universities since late May by exploiting the unpatched Oracle flaw; CISA flagged the bug as posing significant federal-enterprise risk.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (1,000+ orgs; guilty plea)
incidents.vector: Conti ransomware intrusions encrypting data and stealing files to extort victims; defendant coded a malware 'loader.'
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty after extradition from Ireland; Conti hit 1,000+ victims across 47 US states and 31 countries for at least $150M in ransom payments.
